title: Operator claim sandbox and KMS path validator
author: Marta Ruiz
release_notes: Adds an opt-in operator claim sandbox and a KMS path validator that improves auditability and prevents accidental cross-region KMS usage. No user-facing API changes.
description: Context: We continue to see edge cases where operator-scoped claims are used in ways that bypass residency intent checks or produce noisy audit entries. This PR introduces two tightly-scoped pieces of functionality: 1) an operator claim sandbox mode (opt-in) that routes operator-originated requests through a verification layer before they hit policy evaluators; 2) a KMS path validator service that rejects or annotates KMS key paths that indicate cross-region or unsupported provider usage. Motivation: Reduce incident surface from operator impersonation, improve KMS provenance in audit logs, and make policy failures easier to debug without changing the core RBACv2 decision model.

Changes included: checklist, commits summary, changed files list, review conversation and CI summary. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4521) - [x] Unit + integration tests for sandboxed claim flow - [x] E2E test that exercises a KMS path rejection and audit annotation - [x] Docs brief for operator onboarding - [x] Backwards-compatible rollout (feature flag + phased enablement) Commits summary: - 7 commits; top-level: add claims_sandbox controller, add kms_path_validator module, wire sandbox into auth middleware, tests and fixtures, docs and changelog. High-level file changes: - auth/claims_sandbox.go: new controller and feature flag handling - kms/validator.go: path parser and policy rules (provider, region heuristics) - audit/annotator.go: attach kms_provenance hint to audit entries when validator ran - middleware/operator_middleware.go: route operator requests through sandbox when feature flag on - docs/security/operator-sandbox.md: onboarding and troubleshooting - tests/*_sandbox_test.go: unit + integration tests for flows Review thread (abridged): - Arjun Nair: "Can the sandbox path introduce latency for high-volume operator flows?" -> Author: "Sandbox is opt-in and uses async validation for non-blocking fast-path; critical checks are synchronously validated for requests that change residency-scoped resources." - Leah Kim: "Validator heuristics need a whitelist for partner KMS ARNs; otherwise we risk false positives." -> Author: "Added a configurable whitelist and a dry-run mode; updated tests to cover false-positive scenarios." - Connor Blake: "Audit entries must include the validator decision and the rule id so SRE can tune alerts." -> Author: "Audit annotator now attaches kms_validator.rule_id and kms_validator.decision; adjusted schema version to v2-annotated-audit." CI & gating: - Initial pipeline (lint) failed due to import ordering; fixed in commit 4. - Integration suite (policy-e2e) ran in dry-run mode on the feature flag matrix; one flaky test observed (policy cache TTL) which was stabilized by adding a small cache-bust in the test harness. - Final CI status: pass. Observability & metrics: - Added meters: kms_validator.requests, kms_validator.rejections, claims_sandbox.invocations, claims_sandbox.blocked_ops - Tracing: validator emits a trace span kms.validate with attributes (path, provider_hint, decision) Rollout plan: - Feature flag behind org-level rollouts: off by default - Canary: enable for internal admin orgs, monitor kms_validator.rejections and audit growth - If rejections grow unexpectedly, revert to dry-run for that org and open an incident (Linear ENG-4521) Compatibility notes: - No changes to public API surfaces. - RBAC decision flow unchanged; sandbox runs before policy evaluation and can short-circuit only when operator-scoped allowlist/denylist rules are matched. Security rationale: - Prevent accidental cross-region KMS use by making validator decisions explicit and recorded in audit logs - Provide a containment layer for operator claims to reduce blast radius from compromised operator credentials Testing notes: - Unit tests cover region/provider heuristics, whitelist behavior, and parse failures - Integration tests simulate operator requests with a mix of valid/invalid KMS paths and verify audit annotations - Load test (local) shows ~2ms median extra latency for synchronous validation under a 95th percentile optimized code-path; async validation reduces tail latency for no-op checks Documentation: - docs/security/operator-sandbox.md contains admin enablement steps, whitelist format, dry-run behavior and debugging tips. Merge outcome: merged via squash; changelog entry appended. Related work: complements ENG-3703 (policy observability) and SEC-118 (KMS provenance taxonomy). Notes for on-call: If you see a sudden spike in kms_validator.rejections, check the whitelist config and KMS path canonicalization rules (logs include rule_id).
